questions.q: What are the two categories of workflow Purview automates, per this lesson?
options: Data product access workflows, and catalog curation (publish) workflows
Email workflows and SMS workflows
Billing workflows and licensing workflows
Backup workflows and restore workflows
questions.explain: Purview's workflow engine covers approving requests to access data products, and approving data products or glossary terms before they publish to the catalog.

questions.q: What is the first step in starting a new workflow in Purview?
options: A short form — enter a name and an optional description, then select Continue
Writing custom code in a script editor
Contacting Microsoft support to request a new workflow slot
Deleting all existing workflows first
questions.explain: Starting a workflow begins with a short form (name and description) rather than a blank canvas — Continue then opens the actual authoring canvas with a base template loaded.

questions.q: What four-part shape repeats across almost every Purview workflow template?
options: A trigger, a start-and-wait-for-approval step, a condition, then If yes / If no branches
A login screen, a password reset, a logout, and a confirmation email
A backup, a restore, a verification, and a report
A scan, a classification, a label, and a deletion
questions.explain: The default template pattern is: something triggers the workflow, an approval is requested and waited on, a condition checks the outcome, and the flow branches into an approved path and a rejected path.

questions.q: What does the 'Pending on all' approval type require?
options: Every listed approver must approve before the request moves forward
Only the very first approver needs to respond, and the rest are ignored
No approval is required at all — it's fully automatic
The requester has to approve their own request
questions.explain: Pending on all requires every named approver to sign off, appropriate when a decision genuinely needs more than one person's approval.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the risk of choosing 'Pending on all' for a low-stakes request?
options: It slows everyone down waiting for an approver who was never going to object
It automatically rejects the request
It skips the approval process entirely
It grants access without any approver being notified
questions.explain: Requiring every named approver to sign off on something low-stakes adds unnecessary delay when a single qualified approver's sign-off would have been enough.
